transcript.text: Hi everyone! So, as we all know, we want to get together to record some of our older relatives' stories so future family members can listen to them. I've got the only working camcorder, so I'm happy to coordinate the recording evening and handle the files afterward. But before we set a date, let's all agree on the details — things like how long each recording session should be, whether we want video and audio or just audio, and how we'll organize everything on the family drive. What are everyone's thoughts?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should let everyone know — my grandmother told me she's willing to be recorded, but only if the interviews stay in the family archive and are not posted publicly online. I haven't had a chance to mention this to Maya or Omar until now, but I think it's important we all agree to that before we plan the recording evening.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Hey everyone, I actually have something useful to add here. My friend Priya works as an audiovisual archivist, and she gave me some advice about how we should capture the audio for these recordings. She said we should record the audio as uncompressed WAV files at exactly 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, and we should make sure to create two verified backup copies. I think since we're preserving these stories for future family members, it's worth doing it right — so I'd love for us to agree on those specs before the recording evening.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thanks both of you — really glad these things are coming out now so we can agree before the evening. Nina, that's totally reasonable — your grandmother's comfort comes first, so we'll keep all recordings strictly in the family archive with no public posting. I'll make sure that's clear to everyone involved. Omar, those specs sound solid — 48 kHz, 24-bit uncompressed WAV files and two verified backup copies. Since my camcorder captures both video and audio, I want to confirm: are we all on the same page that we want both video and audio for these recordings, not just audio? And does anyone have thoughts on session length — should we aim for, say, 30–45 minutes per relative, with breaks as needed? Once we nail down those last couple of details, I think we'll be ready to settle on a plan and pick a date.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks Maya — I'm glad we're getting all this sorted out before the evening. Video and audio together sounds good to me, and 30–45 minutes per relative with breaks as needed seems reasonable. I'll make sure my grandmother knows the plan before we set the date. I think we're in good shape on the details!
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thanks Maya and Nina! I'm glad we're all on the same page. Just to recap from my side: we'll capture audio as uncompressed WAV at 48 kHz and 24-bit depth, with two verified backup copies, and keep everything in the family archive with no public posting. Video and audio together works for me, and 30–45 minutes per relative with breaks sounds like a solid plan. I think we're in great shape on the details — once Nina's grandmother is on board, we should be ready to pick a date!
